note: Adults enter the Fraser River from April to August (Bradford and Taylor 2023, p. 131, citing COSEWIC 2018), across the region's spring and summer runs, so the start is the region's, not Swift Creek's. The window ends the day before NuSEDS's median start of spawning (08-11), as BULK's migration ends where its spawning starts; NuSEDS's median stream arrival is 08-01 (125 population-years, 1967-2000). NuSEDS's start of spawning is an estimate, not the first spawner seen: read as the bulk of spawning it is 08-12, and 11 records whose survey of three or more visits began before the start put it at 08-15 (research/nuseds_timing.md, #256).

NuSEDS release 20260601: median START_SPAWN_DT_FROM to median END_SPAWN_DT_TO (else END_SPAWN_DT_FROM) over 123 and 126 population-years, 1967-2000, of the populations on streams wholly in UFRA by FWA watershed code, plus the Fraser mainstem above Tete Jaune (data-raw/timing_nuseds.R, scripts/logs/timing/20261118_timing_nuseds.txt). Swift Creek alone 08-09 to 09-05 (27 years); the mainstem above Tete Jaune ends later (median 09-20, 15 years). No START_SPAWN_DT_FROM or end of spawning after 2000 (peaks run to 2014, below). Candy et al. 2002 (Appendix 1) give 2001 peak spawning weeks of 8/16-8/23 at Swift Creek to 8/31-9/7 on the Fraser at Tete Jaune. NuSEDS's start and end dates are estimates, not the first and last spawners seen (83 of the 124 starts NuSEDS gives, one only as a bin's last day, fall on DFO's five-day grid, and 28 of the 76 with a survey's first day precede it), so they support the middle of this window and cannot test its edges. Read as the bulk of spawning (bins as midpoints, records whose adults were present) it runs 08-12 to 09-05 over 124 and 126 population-years (1967-2008), peaking about 08-24 (172 peaks, 1967-2014); its start of 08-15 rests on 11 records whose survey of three or more visits began before it (scripts/logs/timing/20261124_timing_nuseds.txt, research/nuseds_timing.md, #256).
